### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Question

Hi!

I'm not sure when this started happening, but currently I'm on `0.12.4` and using this configuration: https://github.com/aorith/neovim-flake/tree/master/nvim

If I open neovim and do a `Pick grep_live` search (I have it mapped to `space + fg`), then I search for something, for example "transparency" which has a single match... Instead of going to the line 219 of `nvim/init.lua` the cursor stays at line 28 (I have seen it sometimes on line 40)

It is really weird. I tried disabling an [autocmd to restore the last cursor position](https://github.com/aorith/neovim-flake/blob/424e610ba533f35cff8503aae551e671489afb9f/nvim/init.lua#L172-L186) which I had for a looong time, but that didn't solve it, also AFAIK mini.pick changes the cursor synchronously after that.

Then I started disabling other plugins too... without success.

I'm not sure what is going anymore!
Does anyone have an idea?

comment_data.body:
This sounds strange and I indeed can reproduce with the following minimized setup:

- Use clean repro config with this `init.lua`:

    ```lua
    vim.o.splitkeep = 'screen'
    vim.o.showtabline = 2
    vim.pack.add({ 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim' })
    require('mini.pick').setup()
    ```

- At the root of `https://github.com/aorith/neovim-flake` execute `:Pick grep pattern='misc'` and choose the only match in `nvim/plugin/99_mappings.lua` on line 195. It will open the file but put cursor on line 56. Similar behavior for `pattern='Transparency'` and the same line 56, which is somewhat close (but not quite) to the actual height of the Neovim instance.

I haven't yet been able to localize this further. Will take a look later.

comment_data.body:
Okay, it was very much an advanced exercise of figuring out a minimal reproduction example. This resulted in neovim/neovim#40964.

I'll wait a bit for what upstream will do here, but everything points out that this is not a 'mini.pick' issue. And although it (probably) can account for it, I'd rather have this fixed upstream and point users to the new Neovim version.
